about: How much video each Apple chip's H.264/HEVC encode engines take in real time, for `estimate_capacity` (crates/isocast-engine/src/estimate.rs). A file's encoder runs on one engine for its whole life. Rates are 8-bit HEVC pixels a second per engine at Isocast's settings (real-time mode, no B-frames, constant quality), on synthetic content. Add a chip by measuring it (docs/notes.md, #66): record files of known sizes on it and find where ISO files start dropping.

codec_cost.basis: measured with `isocast tune` on isocast-m2-b (hard content, HEVC program): the same ISO files ran 1.28x real time as HEVC and 0.72x as H.264 (4K60 ISO), 1.04x and 0.60x (4K60 + 1080p60 ISOs), so an H.264 picture costs 1.90-1.96x an HEVC one; the stream's H.264 encode is counted the same, though its bitrate-limited real-time encode hasn't been measured on its own

chips.basis: measured on base M2s (isocast-m2-a/b): a 4K60 and a 1080p60 ISO plus a 1080p60 program (747 Mpx/s) record with no drops; adding a 1080p60 stream (983 Mpx/s, its H.264 at 1.9x) or a 4K60 program (1120 Mpx/s) drops frames; `tune` read 1.04x and 0.70x real time for the same files on hard content
measured on an M4 Max (exonbook): two 4K and two 1080p HEVC sessions at 120 fps each (2488 Mpx/s) all hold real time when started apart (#41)
measured on an M5 Max: sixteen 1080p60 HEVC ISO files (1990 Mpx/s) record with no drops; adding the program drops frames
